Top candidates: Stewart's Disease (seedling wilt phase), Goss's Wilt, or Bacterial Stalk Rot.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image for Stewart's Disease (whole plant) shows a near-identical pattern: completely dead, brown/tan plant with all leaves dried out, surrounded by healthy green corn. The match is very strong.

Stewart's Disease causes a seedling wilt phase where individual plants die completely while neighbors remain healthy — exactly what the test image shows.
